name: Open sky
objective: Keep four planets in lasting orbits around one core.
idea: One uninterrupted gravity well. Build separate inner and outer lanes instead of stacking identical shots.
order: Start with a broad orbit, watch it settle, then add planets at different radii. Earlier planets must survive each addition.

name: Neighbouring systems
objective: Establish two orbiting planets around each core.
idea: Two local systems share a boundary. Choose compact orbits that resist the neighbouring well rather than making one large loop around both.
order: Complete the first local system, then build the second. Test the reverse order and long pauses between launches.

name: A common centre
objective: Keep two planets orbiting the entire three-core cluster.
idea: A triangular cluster behaves as one combined field at a distance. Broad enclosing orbits replace separate local pockets. The same two planets contribute to all three core counts.
order: Add one planet outside the entire cluster. Only add its companion after several complete laps around all three cores.
risk: The combined-field orbit must remain outside every enlarged core and be tolerant of launch errors.

name: Giant and companions
objective: Build three orbits around the large well and one around each companion.
idea: An unequal three-body field. The dominant core pulls strongly across two smaller systems, so each region needs a different speed and orbit radius.
order: Populate the dominant well first, then test each companion independently before adding the last planet.
risk: Core size and attraction strength are separate authoring choices; this sketch proposes unequal strengths, pending simulation.

name: The shield
objective: Maintain three orbits beside a repelling obstacle.
idea: One offset repeller removes a quadrant of usable space. Build asymmetric orbits on the open side of the attractor.
order: Establish the inner orbit first, then add wider paths that curve away from the shield. A close pass is not enough to win.

name: Long channel
objective: Keep three planets orbiting through a narrow channel.
idea: Opposing repellers compress the usable field sideways. Long vertical loops demand a different speed profile from an open circular system.
order: Place one elongated orbit through both open ends, then add the next two with generous spacing.
risk: Elongated loops are intended shapes, not simulated trajectories. Repeller strength needs tuning for bounded, forgiving paths.

name: Three harbours
objective: Establish a lasting orbit in each of the three outer wells.
idea: A central repeller separates three attractive harbours. Unlike the shared triangular field, the centre is forbidden and each planet stays local.
order: Fill the easiest harbour, pause, then work around the central barrier one harbour at a time.
risk: Verify full loops in each harbour without a core or repeller obstructing the visible orbit.

name: The divide
objective: Maintain two planets on each side of the repeller wall.
idea: A continuous repelling spine separates two systems. Tight local trajectories must avoid both the wall and the outside edge.
order: Build one side completely before crossing to the other. The wall should make the two systems readable without requiring timed shots.

name: Open crown
objective: Build four lasting orbits inside an open repeller crown.
idea: Five repellers form a shelter with one broad entrance below. Use that opening to populate the sheltered well, without turning the level into a timed gate.
order: Start with the most compact orbit inside the crown. Add broader orbits through the opening after the existing system settles.
risk: Every completed path must return through the opening and remain bounded, rather than escaping after a single pass.

name: Closed garden
objective: Sustain four planets inside the surrounding repeller ring.
idea: A closed six-sided enclosure changes the field in every direction. It creates a compact orbital garden rather than the open crown’s one-sided escape route.
order: Launch inside the enclosure. Start with modest power and add one planet per settled orbit.
risk: Check that repellers create a usable stable band instead of an excessively narrow speed requirement.

name: Broken necklace
objective: Keep two planets in full orbits around both attractive cores.
idea: An alternating five-body necklace combines two attractive wells with three repellers. Outer shared paths must balance both kinds of field, not simply circle an isolated centre.
order: Establish one orbit enclosing both attractive wells and all repellers, then add the second after several complete laps.
risk: An outer shared family must be validated against the repellers’ net outward force and the supported camera bounds.

name: Uneven constellation
objective: Establish one stable local orbit around each of four wells.
idea: Four wells form an irregular chain with unequal gaps. Each local orbit experiences a different neighbouring pull; one repeated launch recipe should not solve every position.
order: Work from the most isolated end toward the denser middle. Verify every earlier orbit survives while completing the chain.
risk: Local lanes need physical clearance and a forgiving speed range around all four cores.
